column1: # Container API of java.util (JRE 1.6) for the container access pattern of Cut-Shortcut (M18, Ma et al. PLDI'23 §3.3, §4.3).
# Source: the Entrance/Exit/Transfer relations of the paper, written out for the JRE 1.6 classes used by Qilin's benchmarks
# Hashtable, TreeMap, TreeSet, PriorityQueue). A method matches by sub-signature when it is declared in a java.util class.
#   views: COL (a collection), MAP (a map), KEYS / VALUES / ENTRIES (views of a map), ENTRY (a Map.Entry); iterators carry
#          the view of the collection they come from; * — any view
#   ENTRANCE: k:CHAN — the k-th argument becomes an element of channel CHAN of the host (ELEM = the element channel of the view:
#             COL -> E, KEYS -> K, VALUES -> V)
#   EXIT:     CHAN — the return value is an element of that channel of the host
#   TRANSFER: VIEW — the returned object depends on the same host with view VIEW (SAME — the receiver's view)
#   ENTRANCE_ALL: k — every element of the hosts of the k-th argument becomes an element of the host (addAll, putAll, copy constructors)
#   NEUTRAL:  adds no element to the host (reads, removals, sizes, constructors without elements)
# A call on a host (or on an object depending on one) of a method that is in none of these lists excludes the host's class
# added after the comparison with the authors' specification (Tai-e DefaultContainerConfig of the Cut-Shortcut artifact, D67):
# navigable sets, blocking queues and deques, DelayQueue (erased to Delayed), CopyOnWriteArrayList, EnumMap, Properties, ConcurrentMap.replace;
# the variants of ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.DelayedWorkQueue are left out: it is allocated only inside java.util, so it is never a host
# iterators and enumerations (on a collection, on keySet() or values() of a map)
# all elements of another described host (D61); the argument must be described completely, otherwise the receiver's class is excluded
# clone: Qilin models Object.clone() as returning the receiver, so the copy is the same host in the model (D62)
